notes.title: Bug fixes and balance changes
notes.notes:
Hi! Thanks for your continued Word Play bug reports. Here's what's changed in 1.06:

[b]New:[/b]

Added more words to the Word Play dictionary

Added tutorial message if player clicks, but doesn't hold, on refresh button

Diamond Tiles are de-prioritised when typing on the keyboard

[b]Re-balanced:[/b]

Buffed Modifier "Add 3 Bonus Points. Increases by 1 when you add a new tile to the Letter Bag". Now +2 on new tile.

Buffed "If two adjacent tiles share the same letter, both score double", to both score triple

Buffed I, E, and O, and Letter Pair challenges. Now +4, and lock at +40.

Buffed "Add 1 Bonus Points for each unused Upgrade" to be +5

Buffed "Increases by 2 whenever you re-roll the perks" Modifier, to +5

Certain Special Rounds (including Special Tiles Nullified) are less likely to appear

[b]Fixed:[/b]

Fixed bug with "If the last word of the round starts with a Vowel, the perk screen will have four perks to pick from"

Improved "Alphabet Challenge" achievement experience

Improved interaction between ! and Mirror Tiles

Fixed bug with "Y is considered a vowel" and "The lowest-scoring Consonant scores 5x"

Improved clarity of "Swap a tile with a Vowel from the Letter Bag", if you don't have the "Y is a vowel" Modifier

Fixed bug with "Convert a tile into a Wildcard Tile with the same score" upgrade

Fixed visual bug when re-rolling perks while using lowercase accessibility setting

Fixed bug with Modifier "If the last tile is a Vowel, permanently increase its score by 2"

Fixed bug with Modifier "Double the Bonus Points rewards for spelling longer words"

Changed descriptions of Refresh and Hold Zone modifiers to increase clarity

Fixed issue with "After each submission, convert a random unsubmitted tile into a Diamond Tile" sometimes picking Diamond tiles

Improved controller support during Special Round "Can use up to 5 Tiles" (etc)

notes.title: Bug fixes - 1.05
notes.notes:
One last patch for the week! Thanks again for your bug reports

[list]
[*] If you have more than one modifier that lets you refresh for free, only one will be used up
[*] Fixed issue with adding phantom tiles to the letter bag when playing with a controller / Steamdeck
[*] Improved typing support when cycling through multiple letters
[*] Improved typing support for ING and ERS tiles - use Shift + I and Shift + E to input them
[*] Removed automatic typing support for wildcards (use 8 / * to insert manually), to reduce confusion
[*] Changed some random elements to favour player
[*] Fixed issue with saving and loading Special Round "Top 4 Tiles are Locked"
[*] Improved performance when using the Modifier "S and Z can be used interchangeably"
[*] Improved various interactions with mirror tiles, wildcard tiles, and exclamation tiles
[*] [strike]Diamond Tiles that are locked will now retain their progression when unlocked[/strike] - Sorry, this was broken! Will restore in a future patch
[/list]

Thanks!

Mark

notes.title: How to play Word Play in another language
notes.notes:
Word Play is designed and developed to be played in English. Not only is all the text in English, and the dictionary only has English words, but much of the game is specifically and carefully balanced around the unique properties of English words, spelling, letter use, and so on.

However - the game does have a secret way to play with other languages.

This is an advanced, experimental, and largely unsupported way to play the game. Please do not attempt this if you're not familiar with modding games!

Also, please note that this does not work with the pre-release demo version of the game.

With all those caveats out of the way, here's how to play with non-English words.

[h3]Finding Your Save Location[/h3]

First, you'll need to find the folder with your save game in it. Here's where to get it:

[b]Mac[/b]

Users/YourUserName/Library/Application Support/com.GMTK.WordPlay

[b]PC[/b]

YourUserName/AppData/LocalLow/Game Maker's Toolkit/Word Play

You may need to show hidden files or folders to get here!

[h3]Making a Custom Dictionary[/h3]

Inside this folder, create a text file called customdictionary.txt

The text file should contain every word that you want the game to accept, in CAPITAL LETTERS, and in alphabetical order. You can include non-Latin characters.

For instance, if you wanted to create a German dictionary you might make a file starting with...

AACHEN
AACHENER
AACHENERIN
AACHENERINNEN
AACHENERN
AACHENERS
AACHENS
AALÄHNLICH
AALÄHNLICHE
AALÄHNLICHEM
AALÄHNLICHEN
AALÄHNLICHER
AALÄHNLICHES
AALANGELFISCHEREI

You should be able to find word lists online - try a search like "German word list Github" or "plain text German word list".

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45595259/aadba8748ba6fa7bf512c0a32ed8bc9450a750ef.png"][/img]

When you next play Word Play, it will look for this file at the start of the game. You'll know you did it right if you see the tag "Custom Dictionary" in the bottom left corner (see above). Otherwise it will use the standard English dictionary.

[h3]Making a Custom Letter Bag[/h3]

Having a dictionary full of non-English words is one thing - but the game will feel very strange with the English letter bag! For instance - a Z tile is worth 10 points because it's rarely used in English... but it's very common in Czech! And try playing in Hungarian without an Ö Tile!

So, you can also make a custom letter bag, with unique tiles, letter values, and letter distributions. Here's how.

In the same location as before, make a text file called customletterbag.txt

On each line, write a 5 character code.

[list][*]The first character is for the actual letter. For example: A.[/*]
[*]The next two characters must be two digits, that represent the tile's value. For instance, if you want A to score 6 points, write 06.[/*]
[*]The final two characters must be two digits, that say how many of this tile should be in the bag. So if you want 4 A tiles, write 04.[/*][/list]
As an example, the bag for a Czech mod might look like this:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45595259/81386acc322bcd32b388b4bbe4dbe3599dcb5480.png[/img]

Where to get these values? You might get inspiration from an existing word board game that I will not name for legal reasons! See what values and distributions they use in your language and borrow those!

[h3]Errors, Limitations, and Reverting to English[/h3]

As I say, this is a totally experimental and unsupported feature. It's totally possible to break the game if you do not follow the instructions carefully! I did not have time to code in complete error prevention - that's on you!

The game also does not feature every non-Latin character - they will show as a square if not supported.

Finally, if you wish to revert the dictionary or letter bag back to English, simply delete one or both txt files and next time you open Word Play it will be back to normal!

Lemme know how you get on!

Mark

notes.title: Accessibility in Word Play
notes.notes:
Hey!

With Word Play less than one month away, I wanted to check in and talk about an important part of the game: accessibility.

Accessibility refers to options, features, and design decisions that open a game up to people who have specific needs or requirements. And I've tried to pack the game with this stuff so that as many people as possible can enjoy the game.

Let's look at some of the main ones...

[h3]Visual Accessibility[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45595259/757141d2a2722815e2ceddb306992f53e753b004.png[/img]

The options menu features a bunch of ways to make the tiles more readable. That includes...

[list]
[*] Lowercase Letters
[*] High Contrast Colours
[*] Multiple Dyslexia-friendly fonts
[*] Colourful tags on vowels
[/list]

Mix and match them to find a set-up that works for you.

There's also a feature to turn off the spotty animated backgrounds if those prove too distracting.

[h3]Motor Accessibility[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45595259/525c745971198f87bfad5af6b384c7f1832b1c14.png[/img]

Word Play should be effortless to interact with. So with that in mind, I've tried to make the game work across a number of input types. You can play Word Play entirely with...

[list]
[*] A mouse
[*] A keyboard
[*] A controller
[*] A touchscreen
[/list]

The game can be played with a single hand. And while you [i]can[/i] drag and drop tiles, you never [i]need[/i] to do it. For instance - instead of dragging and dropping a tile onto the upgrade card, you can just click the card and then click a tile.

[h3]Other Accessibility[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45595259/9f8c5f3f0b5d8e8a1eb3040e3971b5882a30a514.png[/img]

There are no punishments for taking too long to find a word, pick a perk, or choose your strategy. And there are no modifiers that provide a bonus for playing faster. So take as much time as you need to play.

There is also no punishment for spelling a word incorrectly - and the game will even try to suggest a close match word in a little "Did you mean...?" bubble. Handy!

[h3]Difficulty Modes[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45595259/6e935864c81b4f6598a27fd96ac154f36a5c7a37.png[/img]

Word Play can get pretty tricky - just try the Legendary or Marathon modes! But there's also an Easy Mode that's lots of fun too.

Plus - there's the more casual Quick Play mode. This one doesn't require as much strategic thinking, and there's no fixed score requirement to hit - instead, it's just about how many points you can score. The only thing you need to beat is your own high score!

I hope these features will make Word Play more accessible to more people. If you have a certain request or requirement that I might be able to implement [url=https://gamemakerstoolkit.com/gmtk-games/]please get in touch[/url] and I'll see what I can do.

notes.title: What's in the full version?
notes.notes:
Hey! Thanks so much for checking out the Word Play demo.

As you can imagine, the demo only gives you a small sample of what the full game will contain. So here's a rundown of what to expect in the full release when it launches next month.

[h3][b]More Special Tiles[/b][/h3]

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45595259/518df27d62b1a7b7d99a887c83909e0e12884d76.png"][/img]

You've gotten to play with Golden Tiles in the demo, but the full game features a bunch of other upgraded tiles too.

Like Dot Tiles, which double the word's score if used as the final tile. And Diamond Tiles, which power up every time you don't use them. There are others to discover!

[h3][b]More Perks[/b][/h3]

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45595259/d19cbd9079d8a01925160cbec4d4380198f4e57b.png"][/img]

The demo features just 27 perks (that means the modifiers, upgrades, and gifts you can grab when finishing a round). But the full game has over 100 of them!

Want to hold on to some tiles when refreshing? That's a perk. Want a tile that can mirror the letter to its left? That's a perk. Want to permanently destroy tiles? That's a perk!

These perks will change the way you play, open up new strategies and synergies, and create almost infinite replayability.

[h3][b]More Special Rounds[/b][/h3]

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45595259/bc1accbd6b2982258a4687f83cbc64bbafcbd066.png"][/img]

The demo has a few special rounds which force you to play in a specific way - like "Words Shorter Than Six Tiles Score 0 Points" and "Tiles Refresh After Submission".

The full game will have even more devious special rounds to test your spelling skills, and scupper your high score plans!

[h3][b]More Modes[/b][/h3]

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45595259/a620dbcb7ca0351de437c94a787a680c6fc3760b.png"][/img]

The demo gives you access to Word Play's easiest and most basic mode. The full game has a slew of more difficult modes to play (just try and beat Legendary mode!), plus a daily challenge, and more.

[h3][b]More Music[/b][/h3]

The amazing composer Zach Jones (who did the music for [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2685900/Mind_Over_Magnet/https://"]Mind Over Magnet[/url]) has composed a brilliant soundtrack for this game. You can hear a couple tracks in the demo but the full score will be heard in the final game.

[h3][b]More More![/b][/h3]

The full game will also have Steam achievements, Steam Cloud support, and more quality of life and accessibility features.

There will also be more words in the dictionary. If you spell a word that's not in the Word Play dictionary, you can hit a button in game to petition for me to add it. I've already implemented some of the words you've suggested, including ZOOMER, OUIJA, VAPE, EMOJI, and WIFI. More will be added before the final release!

[h3][b]But When?![/b][/h3]

Word Play will be released in July. [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3586660/Word_Play/"]If you add the game to your wishlist[/url] you'll get an email when the game goes live - and you can also take advantage of the launch week discount. But you should also subscribe to Game Maker's Toolkit on YouTube - I'll release a video when the game is released.

[h3][b]Future Plans[/b][/h3]

Don't worry - I've heard your requests for translated / localised versions of Word Play. I'd love to support this but as a solo developer I have to focus exclusively on the English version for launch. After that - I'll see what I can do. Even if it's just helping people mod additional dictionaries into the game.

And I've also heard your requests for a mobile version! And I totally agree - that's why Word Play will be released on iOS later this year, and Android sometime after that. As for consoles (it sure would be nice on that Switch 2 screen...), we'll have to wait and see.

notes.title: 20,000 Demo Downloads! Thanks for Trying Word Play!
notes.notes:
Hey, Mark here.

I just wanted to give a huge thank you to everyone who has tried the Word Play demo, and wishlisted the game on Steam. The demo has been downloaded more than 20,000 times and the game has almost 20,000 wishlists which means it's in a great position for launch.

Speaking of which... I'm planning to launch the game in June, shortly after Steam Next Fest ends. So that means I've got a few more weeks to make the rest of the game! Gulp!

What's in the rest of the game? Well... the demo has just one difficulty mode and about 25 perks (i.e the modifiers, upgrades, and gifts). The final game has more rounds, over 100 perks, more special rounds, more music, more skins, more everything! I hope you're excited to check it out.

I've seen all your feedback on Discord, Bluesky, YouTube, my email inbox, and the Steam forum, and I'm working hard to implement it. Going forward it would be awesome to put it [url=https://discord.gg/BTeTcGA2jc]in this new public Discord forum[/url] so I can more easily track your issues, requests, bugs, ideas, and... of course... words that you totally think should be in the dictionary!

I know that a common request is a translated / localised version of the game. I don't have any immediate plans to offer a non-English version, but I'll see what I can do after launch. It's not impossible, but I am just one man!

I did notice a few bugs, so I just pushed version 1.01 of the demo with a few fixes:

[list]
[*] You can no longer trigger infinite refreshes with a controller!
[*] The "If the word has two of the same letters next to each other..." modifier now works properly
[*] The Glass Tile no longer causes tiles to bug out
[/list]

Anyway, thanks again! 

See you soon,

Mark Brown
Game Maker's Toolkit
